cards.prompt: The Federation signed the expulsion order. We have one dock, no water, and no army.
Federation crews are painting over our port code before the last shuttle leaves.
Our treasury holds eleven weeks of oxygen credits. The public expects a founding celebration.
Sign this transitional charter and the Federation will guarantee your air for five years.
We need a founding signal by midnight. A lion is obvious. Perhaps obvious is useful.
Three patrol ships offer recognition if we let them dock armed and uninspected.
Citizens ask whether independence is courage or a clerical mistake with excellent branding.
Half my class expects evacuation. The other half has started selling evacuation maps.
Dock crews will accept wage restraint if ministers publish their own ration allowances.
The constitution is twelve pages. Arden wants emergency authority on page thirteen.
The upper ring calls us temporary settlers. We have lived here for three generations.
Foreign desks want proof we will honour Federation debts we did not negotiate.
Deck 12 leaks oxygen through bedroom walls. Patch it, or clear it for tower habitats?
Your new towers are clean. They are also six transit gates from our jobs.
Private landlords can build faster, provided we stop asking how many bunks fit in an airlock.
Couples delay children because nursery cabins cost more than a cargo berth.
Habitat ballots keep placing ministers' cousins beside the best oxygen gardens.
The tower plan erases the old market where four home codes share one lunch table.
The crater is empty, ugly, and cheap. I want factories there before investors believe in us.
The first factory offers ten thousand jobs and gloves rated for decorative radiation only.
My assembly line makes mosquito drones. Nobody wants them, but everybody needs a job.
Cargo automation triples throughput. It also makes my entire shift historically interesting.
We can keep wages low for a decade, or tax the port to fund productivity grants.
Declare the lower dock a tax-free zone. Customs officers can enjoy the upper dock.
The ice pipe stays open if your foreign policy stays quiet.
We can drill comet ice locally. The survey says mostly rock and one very confident intern.
Upper rings water gardens at noon. Deck 12 queues for cups before dawn.
The pipeline price is fixed for sixty years. The inspection schedule is, regrettably, creative.
Greywater can flush every tower. Citizens object to pipes labelled 'probably not drinking.'
I found twelve tankers of unregistered ice. The serial numbers appear emotionally unavailable.
A rumour says synth citizens poisoned the tank. The crowd wants an arrest by morning.
cards.historicalInspiration: Communal tension and rule of law

cards.prompt: District feeds translate Arden's speech into eight codes and eight different threats.
The dock strike blocks oxygen filters. Breaking it is easy. Rebuilding trust is not quoted.
School cafeterias segregate by species because lunch has become constitutional theory.
Security has a list of inflammatory poets. Venn is flattered and legally concerned.
The upper ring wants a founders' holiday. The lower deck wants working oxygen seals.
A minister's cousin won every habitat contract. The files are ugly.
Pay inspectors market salaries, or enjoy the efficient private tax they collect under tables.
A modest facilitation fee can move the crater permits before the crater cools.
My office can report to Parliament, or directly to Arden. One is slower. One is Arden.
Investors dislike corruption. They also dislike public procurement taking longer than lunch.
Everyone knows which customs gate never scans. Everyone includes customs.
A professional fleet bankrupts us. Citizen service scares parents. Pick one.
The cadets march well. Their parents march louder and directly toward Parliament.
A neighbour offers pilots, ships, and strategic advice pronounced with ownership.
Rao wants detention without trial for suspected vacuum saboteurs.
Pirates avoid armed docks. They also sell the least expensive armed-dock insurance.
Schools can teach emergency response or another year of mathematics. The vacuum grades harshly.
The imperial garrison leaves next year. Their shields, payroll, and dock contracts leave too.
Thirty thousand garrison jobs vanish at sunrise. The farewell band has been fully funded.
The empty naval yard could become a container port or the galaxy's largest memorial carpark.
Thorn will leave us three shield frigates if we inherit their maintenance debts.
Imperial families request priority berths before departure. Local cargo requests the same berths now.
Garrison stores are being sold by weight. Several officers have developed very heavy pockets.
Children speak eight home codes. Factories want one working code by graduation.
cards.historicalInspiration: Common working language and multilingual education

cards.prompt: Universities teach orbital philosophy. The port needs welders who can keep philosophy pressurized.
Common code works. Grandparents now receive birthday wishes in excellent industrial grammar.
Import engineers now, or wait twelve years for our very promising seven-year-olds.
Top students can receive public scholarships. They must return before the city becomes pleasant.
Workers will attend night school if shifts end before the second artificial sunrise.
My corporation will build a quantum fab. Tax relief, legal stability, no union surprises.
Port AI can clear cargo before it arrives. Customs calls this metaphysically suspicious.
Finance towers pay twenty times dock wages and consume significantly less oxygen per opinion.
Biofabrication firms want public research, private patents, and gratitude from both.
A sovereign fund could invest port surpluses. Arden suggests a board of people who agree with Arden.
Crypto-comets promise a reserve currency immune to governments and occasionally arithmetic.
Your old ice treaty expires early if our inspectors receive permanent access.
Recycled water is purer than imports. The public calls it toilet ice.
Four sources can close the water loop. The fourth is expensive atmospheric condensation.
Local food vats guarantee supply. Imported cuisine guarantees citizens continue eating food.
cards.historicalInspiration: Resource security in an open economy

cards.prompt: Aster-built shield cores cost twice as much and disclose only our own design flaws.
Self-reliance posters now imply foreign lunch is a security vulnerability.
Arden's hands shake. The city trusts him more than the constitution.
I can retire after one final emergency. Conveniently, Rao has found one.
Arden's allies own half the advisory boards. Legal, disclosed, and still half.
Parliament proposes an Arden statue taller than the building containing Parliament.
The next cabinet is competent, dull, and unable to make crowds chant anything useful.
The transition may invite attack. I can place the vote under military protection.
Aster Lion requests Tier-One recognition. Show us a city, not a miracle cult.
cards.historicalInspiration: Recognition as a developed, durable state

cards.prompt: Your water is independent. Is your public information equally clean?
Security is impressive. Please explain why the poets whisper.
The skyline is extraordinary. The queue for Deck 12 housing is also visible from orbit.
Foreign capital built much of this city. Which parts still answer to citizens?
One final question: if Arden vanished from every screen, what would still work tomorrow?
A ration queue becomes a march. The march has discovered the oxygen exchange.
Markets freeze between two price ticks. Payroll becomes a historical document.
Three unidentified drones cross the habitat ring. One broadcasts an apology.
The neighbour closes the ice pipe for maintenance and opens negotiations for convenience.
The emergency procurement server accidentally publishes every minister's private commission.
A recycling membrane ruptures. The clean reservoir now tastes legally ambiguous.
